# The diagnostic catalogue is Gearbox's own, and points at the runtime rather than deriving from it

**ID**: `cpt-gearbox-adr-diagnostic-catalogue-boundary`

## Table of Contents

<!-- generated by `cfs toc` -->

## Context and Problem Statement

`gears-rust` has a canonical error framework, and a good one:
`libs/toolkit-canonical-errors` declares sixteen AIP-193 categories with GTS
identifiers, rendered on the wire as RFC 9457 `application/problem+json`, with a
per-domain typed layer via `#[derive(ContractError)]`. It is documented at
length, referenced across several hundred source files, and treated as a stable
contract.

Gearbox declares seventy-five diagnostic codes of its own in
`crates/gearbox-ir/src/diagnostics.rs`. Two catalogues of "things that went
wrong", in two repositories, one of which is the platform the other composes.
The obvious question follows: should the second be built on the first?

It should not, and the reason is not ownership or convenience. It is that the
two describe different objects, and the difference is load-bearing.

### What each one models

A `CanonicalError` is **a response to a request that failed at run time**. Its
fields say so: an HTTP status, a `trace_id`, an `instance`, a category from a
fixed set of sixteen chosen to map onto gRPC codes. It answers "what should the
caller be told, and what should they do about it now".

A Gearbox diagnostic is about **a description that has not been built yet**. Its
fields say that just as plainly: four severities, an LSP range in a `.gdl` file,
related locations, a `NodeId` subject so a client can select the thing complained
about, a remedy that every error must carry, and a citation into `gears-rust` for
every claim about the runtime.

The two field sets barely intersect. A grep for `severity`, `remedy` or `help`
across all eight files of `toolkit-canonical-errors` returns **zero** hits, and
there is no span, no related location and no subject anywhere in it. Those are
not omissions over there — a runtime error has no source span, because by then
there is no source.

### Why the mapping loses

Sixteen categories cannot carry seventy-five composition-time distinctions. "GDL
parse error", "two REST hosts in one process" and "a plugin fills a point its
host does not declare" would all arrive as `InvalidArgument` or
`FailedPrecondition`. The code *is* the payload here: it is what the lock
records, what the UI keys on, what the documents cite, and what a person greps
for. Folding it into a category and a free-text `detail` would move the meaning
into the prose, which is the one place nothing can check it.

There is an ownership argument too, and it is real but secondary: `gears-rust` is
not this project's to reshape (ADR-0010), and taking a dependency on its error
crate would put the composer's vocabulary on the platform's release cycle.

## Decision Outcome

**The catalogue stays Gearbox's own. It links to the runtime instead of deriving
from it.**

`DiagnosticCode::prevents` names the `gears-rust` runtime error a
composition-time check exists to pre-empt, as
`(package, enum, variant)` plus the frozen `(error_domain, error_code)` pair
where the failure travels on the wire.

Three things about the shape are decisions rather than details.

**It is on `DiagnosticCode`, not on `Diagnostic`.** Every GBX0508 ever emitted
prevents the same failure, so this is a property of the code and not of the
occurrence. On `Diagnostic` it would be a per-call-site string ninety-four
emitters retype — which is exactly how `evidence` came to rot. It also keeps the
change free: `DiagnosticCode` serialises as its string form, so nothing crosses
to TypeScript, nothing changes in the lock, and no existing `lock_hash` is
invalidated. `make ts-check` was run against the empty catalogue for no other
reason than to prove that.

**The reference is a name, not a location.** `path:line` is what `evidence`
already is, and a line number is the part that rots first: a file moves and the
citation is wrong while every identifier in it is still correct. A package name,
an enum identifier and a variant identifier are the three strings a *rename* has
to touch, and a file move touches none of them. A package name rather than a
directory for the same reason `sdk = cargo(...)` names a crate — and because
`gears-rust` declares two enums called `RegistryError`.

**Resolution happens at test time, never at load time.** The engine never reads
`gears-rust` for this, so "no source root open" is not a degradation case; it
cannot arise. `gearbox-project`'s corpus test resolves every reference against
the checkout and skips loudly when none is reachable, with
`GEARBOX_CORPUS_REQUIRED=1` turning the skip into a failure for runs that are
meant to be authoritative.

### The column is optional, and that is deliberate

`requires_evidence` is a bool on all seventy-five codes because "does this assert
a runtime limitation?" is a policy question every code must answer. "Which
runtime error does this prevent?" is not. Most codes prevent no single named
error, and a mandatory column would assert that somebody considered and cleared
all of them.

`Prevents::Nothing` is therefore an **answer**. Two entries make that concrete
and should stay unconverted:

* **GBX0503** — its own text says "a silent correctness failure at runtime rather
  than a startup error". There is no error to name. Inventing one would be worse
  than saying nothing.
* **GBX0409** — the failure is a key that silently fails to match inside
  `remap_gear_env_key`, a *function*. This marks the boundary: `Prevents`
  references runtime errors, not arbitrary Rust items.

The cost of optional is that "explicitly nothing" and "not yet considered" look
alike. That is paid by a reverse guard: once any code references an enum, a doc
comment naming `ThatEnum::Something` without its own `prevents` fails a test. Its
allow-list starts empty, so an exception has to be written down.

### The catalogue is documented, generated

The GDL reference described seventeen of the codes in a hand-written table with no
drift guard, and `DiagnosticCode::title()` had no caller outside its own test: it
was declared for a reference page nobody built. `make diagnostics` now generates
`docs/diagnostics.md` from `DiagnosticCode::ALL`, guarded by
`make diagnostics-check` exactly as the editor's grammar vocabulary is. The
curated table in the GDL reference, `docs/gdl.md`, stays hand-written, because it
carries a column — which stage reports the code — that the catalogue does not
know.

### Not localized

Neither repository is localized, and this one already carried the decision in a
comment (`ide/gearbox-studio/src/browser/start/start-widget.tsx:271-277`): *"the
shell is not localised and one English sentence beats a locale-shaped guess"*.
It is recorded here so the question stops being reopened.

`gears-rust` hard-codes English titles as `&'static str` and composes `detail` at
the call site, with no message-id indirection and no `Accept-Language` handling
anywhere; its only translation infrastructure serves the documentation website.
So localizing Gearbox's half would leave the other half English regardless —
evidence strings are paths into that repository, and the runtime errors a
diagnostic references have no other language to be asked for.

Beyond that: the stable interface here is the **code**, not the text. The
messages are dense technical prose interleaved with identifiers, config keys and
paths, built with `format!` at eighty-two of the ninety-four construction sites.
And the present cost is not small — roughly forty-nine `message.contains(...)`
assertions, one `insta` snapshot pinning full message text, two production sites
in `gearbox-gdl` that classify Starlark failures by sniffing strings, and one UI
site where the message *is* an identity key
(`ide/gearbox-studio/src/browser/add-gear/impact.ts`, keyed on
`` `${code}|${message}` ``).

The door stays open at no cost, which is why this is a "not now" and not a
"never": the code is already a stable key with a single home, so a bundle keyed
by code can be added later, additively, with today's string as the fallback. What
would have to be settled first is `impact.ts`, whose identity key would become
locale-dependent — one file, not a migration.

## Consequences

* A rename in `gears-rust` fails a Gearbox test instead of quietly making a
  document wrong. That is the whole point, and it is also the cost: a platform
  refactor now has a downstream consumer that notices.
* The corpus test walks about a hundred and twenty `Cargo.toml` files and parses
  two crates. Measured at roughly 0.8 s, run once, in `gearbox-project`'s test
  binary only.
* Two catalogues remain, and a reader has to know that one describes composition
  and the other describes requests. The `prevents` column is what makes the
  relationship between them legible rather than folklore.
* `evidence` is not replaced. A `path:line` is still right where the thing being
  cited is a line of code rather than a named error, which is most of the
  twenty-three cases.

## Confirmation

* `crates/gearbox-ir/tests/diagnostics.rs` — references are well formed, and
  prose naming a watched enum must declare a column. Neither needs a checkout,
  so both run everywhere.
* `crates/gearbox-project/src/error_enum_corpus_tests.rs` — every reference
  resolves. Verified by tampering rather than by assertion alone: a wrong
  variant, a wrong enum, and a wire code moved to a different variant were each
  made to fail, and the last produced its intended sentence, "the local error
  and its wire twin have stopped agreeing".
* The same file's `decide` — whether a missing checkout skips or fails — is a
  function so that the arm no machine with a checkout can reach is still tested.
  An unreachable arm deciding whether a suite reports anything is the kind that
  stops working unnoticed, which is the failure `test_corpus` was written about.
* `make ts-check` and the `gearbox-lock` golden snapshot, both unchanged, are the
  evidence for the "no wire impact" claim above.
* `make diagnostics-check` — the reference cannot fall behind the catalogue.

## Traceability

* Strengthens `cpt-gearbox-nfr-evidence-cited` (`docs/PRD.md:840-845`), which is
  amended to add the typed tier beside the `path:line` one.
* Serves `cpt-gearbox-nfr-actionable-diagnostics` (`docs/PRD.md:896-902`)
  indirectly: the generated reference is where a code's explanation is now
  readable outside Rust.
* Applies `cpt-gearbox-nfr-no-type-drift` to the documents' view of the
  catalogue, as `make grammar-check` applies it to the editor's view of the
  language.
* Follows ADR-0002's rule (`docs/ADR/0002-cpt-gearbox-adr-macro-projected-catalogue.md`):
  the facts are read out of Rust with `syn` rather than restated, and what the
  description supplies is a locator.
* Respects ADR-0010's tiers: `gears-rust` is read and never written.
